veio.guide.title: Veio Field Guide
veio.guide.welcome: The village needs a workshop. Follow the objective above the hotbar. The workbook is an optional reference; tutorial progress follows working machines.

veio.componenthelp.iron_plate: Press raw iron. Used for frames and steel.

veio.guide.page.02:
Technical reference

To learn automation, use Your first workshop: book + cobblestone.

The Factory board tracks phases and deliveries. Find machines, power, logistics and recipes here.
veio.guide.page.03:
When a machine stops

No power: check fuel and cables.

No ore: check the block underneath.

Missing material: inspect the slots.

Output full: make room downstream.
veio.guide.page.04:
Controls and help

Empty hand + right-click opens the panel.

Wrench + right-click turns it.

Hover over ? or an empty slot for help.

Powered redstone pauses production.
veio.guide.page.05:
Your checklist

Open Advancements and find First requests. Milestones track obtained materials.

Pick up products to mark progress.

Inspect machine panels to confirm operation.
veio.guide.page.06:
Poles and wires

Each pole powers machines within 2 blocks (steel: 3) and links to nearby poles.

Wood: 8-block wire, 120 FE/t.
Steel: 16-block wire, 400 FE/t.

Starving far away? The wire is the limit.
veio.guide.page.07:
Pollution

Working machines pollute their chunk; the panel shows how much per minute. It spreads and slowly fades.

Harvested crops absorb it. Efficiency modules halve it.
veio.guide.page.08:
Raiders

Chat warns a day ahead. The next night they come with a raid horn, for you and the villagers.

Four hits stop a machine or kill a villager. Walls, a sword, barracks and Tesla towers.
veio.guide.page.09:
Modules

Right-click a machine to install one. Sneak with the wrench to remove it.

Speed: more output, power and pollution.
Efficiency: less power and pollution.
Productivity: +20% products.
veio.guide.page.10:
Factory and world

Harvester: build the farm around it and belt the crops away.

Tesla tower: guards the base at night. Pair solar with batteries.

Monster bones become bone meal in the crusher.
veio.guide.page.11:
Trade

After the village project, the hub keeps exporting: 4 circuits and 4 steel plates become 4 emeralds and 2 experience bottles.
veio.guide.page.12:
Production ladder

Each upgrade fixes one bottleneck and reveals the next: vein, power, wire, pollution.

Connected veins pay off: 7+ linked ore blocks double the speed, 16+ quadruple it.
veio.guide.page.13:
Optional beacon

After the village project, empty the hub inputs. Put 1 Nether star in input 1 first, then 48 circuits in input 2.

Receive 1 beacon and 2 Mk.II extractors. Clear the outputs: the grand project comes next.

veio.guide.page.16:
Rivers and dams

In new terrain, springs high in the mountains form rivers that run to the sea, join and grow, with falls on the way.

Close a valley and set the turbine in the wall: a higher drop and a wider lake pay more. So does a big river.
veio.guide.page.17:
Food and village

Wheat > mill > flour > kitchen > bread.
Ranch meat > electric furnace.

The pantry pays emeralds for food, more for cooked food, and 50% more with villagers near.
veio.guide.page.18:
The worker village

Hired villagers work for you: fields, animals, machines, storage and a control center.

It is all in the Worker Village Guide, given when you obtain a post. Book + wheat craft another.
veio.guide.page.19:
Input and output

GREEN (front and sides): the machine takes items.
RED (back): products leave; nothing enters.

A belt accepts nothing from its front and holds up to 5 ores or 1 finished product (fast 2, express 4).

veio.guide.page.20:
Conveyor turns

Connect one incoming and one outgoing belt. The corner adjusts automatically.

At junctions, use the wrench to lock the outlet. Sneak with it to restore automatic routing.
veio.guide.page.21:
Up and down

Place belts on stair-stepped blocks, one block of height per step.

The lower belt becomes a ramp. Leave headroom.

Machines, splitters and mergers connect at the same height.
veio.guide.page.22:

Copier: build a line on the square above it and click with paper.
Build marker: empty hand lists materials; sneak with the wrench to build.

Floors: a ladder up to the next floor, or a cargo lift.

veio.village.page.02:
The worker village

You start at the center of a village. Villagers start working for you, and the village grows with the factory.

Follow the steps in order. The Worker Village advancement tab tracks progress.
veio.village.page.03:
1. First worker

Farmhand post near crops and villagers.

Bread in the left slot; click the post with an emerald.

The villager harvests and brings the crop back.
veio.village.page.04:
2. Mark the field

Place the field marker at the center of the field, with water nearby.

Posts within 3 blocks of the border work the whole area: till, plant and harvest.

Seed in the marker: only that is planted.
veio.village.page.05:
3. Pens

Fence the animals and put the pen marker in the middle. A nearby shepherd post tends them.

Feed in the marker sets the pen: carrots for pigs, seeds for chickens, wheat for cows and sheep.
veio.village.page.06:
4. Barn and silo

The barn keeps any item; the silo, grain and food.

Hoppers insert and extract. With a foreman nearby, surplus goes there by itself.
veio.village.page.07:
5. Haulers

The hauler post feeds machines within 6 blocks from the left slots and brings products to the right.

It leaves belts alone.
veio.village.page.08:
6. Foreman and queue

The foreman desk manages 6 posts within 12 blocks: brings food and rehires with emeralds.

It queues deliveries between posts, machines and storage, done by haulers.
veio.village.page.09:
7. Control center

Hire an administrator. Three pages (wrench switches): Summary, Attention and Projects.

Item in a goal slot: x16 stored. Book on the center: report. Spawn moves to the center.
veio.village.page.10:
Manage up close

The Attention page lists what stopped, most urgent first. Hover a line: what to do.

Compass on the center: the action bar takes you there and explains. Once solved, the next one comes.
veio.village.page.11:
Requests and prestige

Each morning the village makes 3 requests (center page 4). Deliver in the Build slot: emeralds to the treasury and +10 prestige.

Tiers: Hamlet, Village (60), Thriving (200), Worker city (500).
veio.village.page.12:
Decrees and treasury

Item in the Decree slot:
Bell: hire within 16.
Paper: tasks at 1, no babies.
Hay: tasks at 3, zones double, more babies.

The treasury pays zones and projects. Sneak + emerald: withdraw.
veio.village.page.13:
Bigger projects

Village: Library (zones double) and Post office (4 requests, +50%).
Thriving: Inn (cap +20, travelers).
City: Town hall (prestige +50%, interest).

veio.industry.page.02:
Large-scale industry

With steel, the factory grows by volume: new recipes come from research that asks for hundreds of parts.

Build lines that run on their own and measure each one.
veio.industry.page.03:

veio.industry.page.05:
Ratios

Recipes show items per minute of one machine without modules, and the cycle.

Press: 40 copper > 40 plates
Assembler: 60 plates > 30 gears

Three presses feed two assemblers (120 = 2 x 60).
veio.industry.page.06:
On the panel

Above each slot the panel shows what the machine asks and gives per minute, with module and Mk.II.

Belts: basic 150/min, fast 300/min, express 600/min. Add machines until the belt is full.
veio.industry.page.07:
Deep chain

Motor: steel + 4 wires (integrator)
Processor: 2 circuits + 2 silicon
Core: 2 motors, 2 proc., 4 steel (fabricator)
Mk.II kit: 2 motors, 1 proc., 8 gears

The core feeds the scale research and the grand project.
veio.industry.page.08:
Mk.II kit

Right-click a recipe machine or drill with the kit: half the cycle, double power per tick and 25% more pollution.

It stacks with the module. Sneak with the wrench to remove the module, then the kit.
veio.industry.page.09:
Factory monitor

Shows the machines in the dimension: active, waiting for input and stuck.

Lists the 9 busiest items: made and used per minute. Red usage is short on the line.

Every 30 s it warns where a machine is stuck.
veio.industry.page.10:
Distant outposts

At the outpost: a cargo station at the end of the line. At the base: an unloading station.

Click both with the same dye: that is the channel. Up to 1,200 items/min, 10 FE per item.

The channel holds up to 4,096 items in transit.
veio.industry.page.11:
While you are away

The cargo station measures what it ships per minute. When the outpost unloads it keeps shipping at that rate, loading nothing.

When you return, the outpost resumes. Change the line nearby: the new rate counts after 1 minute.
veio.industry.page.12:
Chunk anchor

To keep a chunk truly alive (machines reacting, villagers, redstone): with 32 FE/t it stays loaded.

Heavier than stations. Without power for 5 s it releases. Broken, in 20 s.
veio.industry.page.13:
New logistics

Tunnel: two facing the same way, up to 6 blocks. Items pass under walls and rails.

Clipboard: sneak to copy an arm or splitter's filter and priority; stand to paste onto another.

Express belt: 10 items/s.
veio.industry.page.14:
Piped lava

A pump touching still lava (and no water) draws 5 mB/t per source.

Pipes carry it to the geothermal generator: 1,000 mB is one bucket, with no empty buckets. Each pipe holds one fluid.
veio.industry.page.15:
Grand project

After the four contracts, the hub asks for the transmission tower in four phases:

1 200 steel, 100 modules
2 300 circuits, 100 motors
3 150 proc., 50 cores
4 200 cores, 50 Mk.II kits

It collects slowly and pays each phase.

8. Homes and families

House: up to 4 villagers within 10 blocks. Workers earn wages; the family eats from the pantry and buys at the shop.

Without food, services or income, HDI drops. Spread districts: crowded homes live worse.
veio.village.page.25:
9. Shop

The merchant is independent. What you deliver to the stock they buy wholesale (75% of price) and pay from sales; without cash, on credit.

Homes buy during the day; you buy by trading with them.
veio.village.page.26:
10. Mayor and accounts

Company (yours): center vault. Pays your workers; receives wholesale.
Town hall: tax withheld at source on every sale (4%, 8%, 12%, 16%). Pays the clerk and assistance.
veio.village.page.27:
Calendar and holidays

6-day seasons; the 6th is Sunday. On 6 holidays a year the village stops and gathers at the plaza.

Two days before, a visitor comes to the town hall: click them and deliver in the Agenda slot.
veio.village.page.28:
Morale and works

Prepared festival: morale up. Empty holiday: down. Morale scales HDI (0.9x to 1.1x).

Park, plaza or monument requests: build the block in the district. The town hall pays.
veio.village.page.29:
Holding

The control center is the company headquarters. The < > arrows switch business: mining, manufacturing, power, logistics, agriculture, forestry, urban, retail and management.

Each tab: units, active, workers, daily output and what is stopped.
veio.village.page.30:
Money

The emerald is the currency: 60 coins each. Money only circulates:
industry → wages → families → shops → wholesale → industry.

It only enters or leaves as real emeralds: deposits, cash outs and your purchases. The town hall report checks the sum.
veio.village.page.31:
Foreign trade

Outside connections: cargo port (on the sea or a wide river) and freight station (at the frontier, 96 blocks from HQ). Haul cargo to them; each trip has capacity and freight.

When food runs short, shops import through them.
veio.village.page.32:
Market and contracts

Quote = value x complexity x the day's market; it drops if you flood an item.

Contracts have deadlines and pay 50% more; chat tells you. Reputation 1 opens components, 3 electronics, 6 modules. A lost contract: -1.
veio.village.page.33:
Local prices

Each shop sets its own prices. High demand and low stock: up to double. Idle stock: drops to 70%. Families who find no food push prices up.

Each village has its own market: supply where it is expensive.
veio.village.page.34:
Phases

1 Hamlet: zone level 2, 30 villagers, 4 homes.
2 Village: 12 residents, 3 families, HDI 0.40.
3 Town: 36, 9, HDI 0.55, GDP 400, jobs 60%.
4 City: 80, 20, HDI 0.70, Gini 0.45, 3 districts.

Homes need a well (phase 2), pole (3) and shop (4).
veio.village.page.35:
Indicators

HDI: food, housing, services and income of each family (0 to 1).
Gini: income inequality.
GDP: tasks done and sales in the last day.
Employment: adults with a post.

Book on the town hall: report with districts and requests.
veio.village.page.36:
Construction site

Pay at the center, then place the site where you want the building: the blue border shows its size, the arrow the door.

Wrench switches blueprint. Hire a master builder and feed him: he raises it.
veio.village.page.37:
Blueprint: Canteen

Brick hall with a kitchen at the back (smokers, cauldron and counter), two long tables for 21 people, candles and a smoking chimney.

11x9, 12 tall.

veio.onboarding.why.0: Every Veio machine needs power. The generator burns coal and sends power through cables.
veio.onboarding.do.0.1: 1. The mayor built your generator. To make more, the recipe is in the recipe book (green).
veio.onboarding.do.0.2: 2. Place the generator on the workshop plot you flattened.
veio.onboarding.do.0.3: 3. Open the generator with an empty hand and put coal in its fuel slot.
veio.onboarding.why.1: The press turns raw copper into plates, but only works with power arriving.
veio.onboarding.do.1.1: 1. The press and the cables come from Seu Bento, the smith, in exchange for a favour (follow the bar). Later you can craft more.
veio.onboarding.do.1.2: 2. Place the press and connect it with touching cables: generator > cable > cable > press.
veio.onboarding.do.1.3: 3. Look at the press marks: GREEN strips take items; the RED frame (back) releases products.
veio.onboarding.do.1.4: 4. The step advances when the press receives power. Open it to see the power bar.
veio.onboarding.why.2: Before automating, see how a machine works: input, progress and output.
veio.onboarding.do.2.1: 1. Mine raw copper: copper ore with a stone pickaxe or better.
veio.onboarding.do.2.2: 2. Open the press and put RAW copper in the left slot (input).
veio.onboarding.do.2.3: 3. Wait for the arrow to fill and take the plates from the right (output).
veio.onboarding.do.2.4: 4. Make 4 new plates. If the machine stops, hover over the panel status: it tells you why.
veio.onboarding.why.3: Factories chain machines: the press plate becomes a gear in the assembler.
veio.onboarding.do.3.1: 1. Craft the assembler (card above) with 2 of your plates.
veio.onboarding.do.3.2: 2. Place it, power it and put 2 plates in its input.
veio.onboarding.do.3.3: 3. Take the finished gear from the output.
veio.onboarding.why.4: Mining by hand does not scale. The extractor mines the deposit on its own, forever.
veio.onboarding.do.4.2: 2. Place it ON TOP of copper ore, without mining it. Bigger vein below = faster.
veio.onboarding.do.4.3: 3. Bring power to it. Copper appears at the output (red frame).
veio.onboarding.why.5: Now the extractor feeds the press: copper travels on its own.
veio.onboarding.do.5.1: 1. Craft belts (card above: each recipe makes 16).
veio.onboarding.do.5.2: 2. The first touches the extractor RED frame. A belt runs AWAY from you.
veio.onboarding.do.5.3: 3. The last one enters a GREEN face of the press (front or side; never the red one).
veio.onboarding.do.5.4: 4. Deliver 2 copper by belt and let the press make 1 plate from them.
veio.onboarding.why.6: A complete line also carries products away. Otherwise the output fills and the machine stops.
veio.onboarding.do.6.1: 1. Craft a chest and place it near the press.
veio.onboarding.do.6.2: 2. Run belts from the press RED frame into the chest: it unloads by itself.
veio.onboarding.do.6.3: 3. Store 4 plates made by the line. Arms, hoppers and haulers also count.
veio.onboarding.why.7: The hub takes village orders and pays in materials: it is your factory goal.
veio.onboarding.do.7.1: 1. Make a gear in the assembler and craft the hub (card above).
veio.onboarding.do.7.2: 2. Gather 24 plates and 8 gears (2 plates each).
veio.onboarding.do.7.3: 3. In the hub: plates in input 1, gears in input 2; keep outputs clear.
veio.onboarding.do.7.4: 4. Reward: 64 belts and 32 cables. Tip: run the press belt into the hub.
veio.onboarding.why.8: The board is the village plan: it shows the phase, the daily order and where your factory got stuck.
veio.onboarding.do.8.2: 2. Place it near the machines: it sees everything within 96 blocks.
veio.onboarding.do.8.3: 3. Open the board: the panel counts machines working, unpowered, blocked and not set up.
veio.onboarding.tip.faces: Tip · Input and output: GREEN strips (front and sides) take items; the RED frame (back) releases products and accepts nothing. A machine never pushes its product onto the belt that feeds it.

veio.wiki.article.start.title: First steps
veio.wiki.article.start.body:
Veio is industrial automation inside Minecraft: mine the world's deposits, turn them into parts and build lines that run on their own.
The on-screen tutorial (above the hotbar) goes from the generator to the first daily order in 16 steps. Each step shows the recipe, where materials come from and a checklist of what you already have.
• 1. Generator with coal  • 2. Press wired with cables  • 3. Plates by hand  • 4. Gear in the assembler
• 5. Extractor on copper  • 6. Belt into the press  • 7. Belt into a chest  • 8. Order at the hub
• 9. Factory board  • 10. First board phase  • 11. Another extractor  • 12. Splitter
• 13. Poles  • 14. Daily order  • 15. Meal at the Home  • 16. Control center
Veio recipes show up in the recipe book (the green book in your inventory) as soon as advancements unlock them.
This wiki opens with J. Click an item to see how to craft it, where it is made and where it is used.
veio.wiki.article.power.title: Power
veio.wiki.article.power.body:
Machines use power (FE). It comes from generators, travels through touching cables or poles with wires and is stored in each machine (up to 2,000 FE) and in batteries.
• Generator: up to 40 FE/t burning furnace fuel (coal 16,000 FE).
• Geothermal: up to 80 FE/t from a lava bucket (64,000 FE); returns the bucket.
• Steam engine: 120 FE/t, double energy per fuel; needs still water beside it.
• Water wheel and wind turbine: up to 32 FE/t, no pollution. Solar: up to 16 FE/t at noon.
• Battery: stores 30,000 FE to get through the night.
• Wooden pole: reaches 8 blocks, powers a radius of 2 and carries 120 FE/t. Steel pole: 16 blocks, radius 3, 400 FE/t.
If a machine says 'no power', check fuel, touching cables and pole reach.
veio.wiki.article.io.title: Input, output and belts
veio.wiki.article.io.body:
Every machine has fixed sides: GREEN strips (front and sides) take items; the RED frame (back) releases products and accepts nothing.
The output faces away from you when you place the machine. The wrench rotates it and keeps its contents.
A belt runs away from you when placed and accepts nothing from its front. So a machine never pushes its product onto the belt that feeds it.
Load per belt block: up to 5 ores (or stone, logs) or 1 finished product (2 on fast, 4 on express). Belts carry; use chests to store.
• Basic: 2.5 items/s  • Fast: 5 items/s  • Express: 10 items/s
Belts turn on their own and climb or drop 1 block per step. The wrench locks direction; sneak with it to go back to automatic.
Splitter: alternates its two side outputs (filter and priority by sneaking). Merger: joins two inputs into one. Tunnel: goes under up to 6 blocks.
Redstone pauses machines, belts and arms.
veio.wiki.article.extraction.title: Deposits and extraction
veio.wiki.article.extraction.body:
The extractor works on top of a world deposit without breaking it: the deposit never runs out.
On ores it measures the vein connected to the block right below it (by faces, in 3D). Normal and deepslate ore count together.
• 1-2 blocks: impure, half speed  • 3-6: normal  • 7-15: pure, double  • 16+: industrial, 4x (double power)
Stone, sand, gravel, clay and other infinite deposits read the 3x3 square below.
Mk.I: 1 unit every 2 s, 6 FE/t. Mk.II: 1 per second, 12 FE/t, and mines diamond and emerald (slowly). Mk.III: 4x Mk.I and ancient debris.
One basic extractor feeds one press. Plan lines in whole-number machine ratios.
veio.wiki.article.chains.title: Production chains
veio.wiki.article.chains.body:
Each machine turns one thing into another. Chained, they become a line.
• Press: raw copper → copper plate; raw iron → iron plate
• Assembler: 2 copper plates → gear
• Cutter: copper plate → wire; iron plate → frame
• Integrator: frame + gear → module; steel + 4 wires → motor
• Alloy furnace: 2 iron plates + coal → steel
• Crusher: quartz → silicon; bone → bone meal; cobblestone → gravel → sand
• Circuit assembler: 2 wires + silicon → circuit; 2 circuits + 2 silicon → processor
• Mill, kitchen and electric furnace: flour, bread, cakes, roasts and glass
A machine waits for materials, power and output space; ingredients are used together at the end of the cycle. Look up each machine for times and FE.
veio.wiki.article.progression.title: Phases and research
veio.wiki.article.progression.body:
The factory advances in phases, as in Satisfactory: within a phase each unlock asks for one part; moving on asks for a stack that only a working line delivers.
• 1 Copper: one copper ingot opens the extractor, press, belts, mill and power.
• 2 Workshop: 32 gears → wrench, crusher, alloy furnace, repair kits, wind turbine.
• 3 Steel: 16 steel plates → battery, geothermal, steam engine, steel pole, forestry, ranch.
• 4 Electronics: 16 circuits → solar, Mk.II extractor, Tesla tower, modules, grow lamp.
• 5 Depth: one installed module → Mk.III.
The Factory board shows the phase, what is missing and the daily orders. The research lab opens Metallurgy, Electronics, Automation and Scale with large part packages.
Advancements (L key) unlock recipes: see the Veio tab for the whole path.
veio.wiki.article.modules.title: Modules and bottlenecks
veio.wiki.article.modules.body:
The factory grows by solving one bottleneck at a time: extraction limits the press, power limits machines, wire limits far power, pollution limits size without defense.
Modules go in by right-clicking a recipe machine or extractor (one each). Sneak with the wrench to take it back.
• Speed: 60% cycle, 180% power, 150% pollution
• Efficiency: 60% power, 50% pollution
• Productivity: +20% (one extra batch every 5 cycles), 115% cycle, 140% power
Each machine panel shows items per minute and active time: use it to find where the line stalls.
veio.wiki.article.transport.title: Transport between zones
veio.wiki.article.transport.body:
To link a far mine to the workshop: rail terminals (chest minecarts and hoppers), drone ports (up to 16 items up to 64 blocks) and caravan terminals (horses, donkeys, mules, pigs).
Click both ends with the same dye to link the route. Sneak with the product that should leave to set the dispatch.
In the panel the three left slots are Dispatch and the right ones Received. Haulers fill Dispatch and empty Received.
Sender and receiver stations link distant posts by channel (dye), at the measured rate even far from you.
veio.wiki.article.workforce.title: Worker village
veio.wiki.article.workforce.body:
Hired villagers work without electricity: they use food and one hiring emerald.
With an emerald in hand, click the post: the nearest free villager (within 8 blocks) is hired.
• Farmer: harvests and replants up to 9x9  • Shepherd: tends, shears and collects from animals
• Hauler: feeds machines within 6 blocks and collects products  • Foreman: feeds, rehires and plans transfers
• Barracks: militia, guard, archer and mage defend the village at night
Food in the left slot: each task costs 2 points (bread is worth 6, cooked meat 8, wheat 1).
Field and pen zones, barn and silo grow by levels. The control center is the headquarters: goals, holding and foreign trade.
Sneak + wrench dismisses the worker. Civilian workers sleep at night.
Village tutorial: after the factory, talk to mayor Otávio (or use /veiotutorial vila). Eight steps: post, hiring, zone, harvest, hauler, foreman, house and town hall.
veio.wiki.article.society.title: Village society
veio.wiki.article.society.body:
House: up to 4 villagers within 10 blocks become a family. Workers earn wages; the family eats from the pantry and buys at the nearest shop.
Shop: hire a merchant and stock it. Prices rise with demand and fall with idle stock; each village has its own market.
Town hall: hire a villager as mayor Otávio's clerk. They measure population, jobs, GDP, HDI and Gini within 128 blocks and unlock the village phases.
• Hamlet → Village (12 residents, HDI 0.40) → City (36, HDI 0.55, GDP 400/day) → Metropolis (80, HDI 0.70, 3 districts)
From phase 2 a new house needs a well within 24 blocks; from 3 also a pole; from 4 also a shop. Too low an HDI suspends new zone levels.
Houses packed together (more than 6 neighbours within 16 blocks) are crowded, and nearby pollution hurts housing: spread districts live better.
Book at the town hall: report with districts, problems and the next phase goal.
Chapter 4, the village grows (/veiotutorial crescer): well, shop, first sale, company account, power, leisure, three families, taxes, a festival and the Village phase. Chapter 6, the city (/veiotutorial cidade): 9 families, jobs, services in every house, a civic work, GDP and the City phase.
veio.wiki.article.economy.title: Economy and money
veio.wiki.article.economy.body:
The emerald is the currency: 1 emerald = 60 coins. Money only circulates; nothing appears or vanishes on its own.
Company (you, in the control center vault) → wages → families → shops (retail) → wholesale → company.
Each sale withholds tax at source for the town hall (4%, 8%, 12% and 16% by phase). The town hall pays the clerk, wells and aid to the poor.
Money only enters or leaves as real emeralds: vault deposits, withdrawals from the panel, your purchases and foreign trade.
The control center shows each holding company (mining, manufacturing, power, logistics, agro...) with revenue, costs and profit.
There is one reference price inside and outside the village (bread is 9). The local price never exceeds the import cost.
veio.wiki.article.trade.title: Foreign trade
veio.wiki.article.trade.body:
The cargo port (on the sea or a wide river, a ship every 2 min) and the cargo station (at the border, a train every minute) sell to the world market.
Quote = value × complexity (1x to 4x) × daily index. Flooding an item drops its quote: diversify.
Freight per stack weighs most on raw materials. Exporting higher value-added goods pays off.
Timed contracts pay 50% more and raise reputation, which opens component, electronics and module markets.
When food runs short, shops import through the connections; the tariff goes to the town hall.
Foreign trade tab at the control center: market, contracts, reputation and what is stuck.
veio.wiki.article.agenda.title: Calendar, holidays and civic works
veio.wiki.article.agenda.body:
The year has 4 seasons of 6 days (24 days). The 6th day of each season is Sunday.
Fixed holidays: Founding (spring 1), Flowers (spring 4), Saint John (summer 3), Harvest (autumn 4), Lights (winter 3), New Year (winter 6). On a holiday the village stops working and celebrates at the plaza.
Two days before, a visitor arrives at the town hall. Click them: they tell you the request. Deliver the materials in the town hall's 3rd slot (Agenda).
Request ready: the town hall reimburses the company and morale rises on the day (+20 to +25). Unprepared holiday: morale −10.
Sundays without a holiday have a fair, a dance or a fishing contest (+8 morale if prepared).
Civic works: every 4 days the mayor asks for a park (240), plaza (420) or monument (720) for the district without leisure. Build it within 32 blocks in 6 days.
Morale (0 to 100) multiplies HDI by 0.9x to 1.1x; leisure counts as an HDI service.
veio.wiki.article.defense.title: Pollution and defense
veio.wiki.article.defense.body:
At night monsters hunt whoever is outside: the village shuts in at the bell. Light (torches) stops monsters spawning; a wall with a gate keeps them out; sleeping skips the night. Tutorial chapter 2: /veiotutorial noite.
Machines pollute their chunk: generator 6/s, alloy furnace and Mk.II 4, extractor, crusher and geothermal 2, others 1. Pollution spreads and 2% fades each step.
Above 400, chat warns you. A day later, at night, with the most polluted chunk above 1,200, Raiders come (4 the first night, up to 12).
They attack whoever is at the factory, then the barracks defenders, the villagers and finally the machines.
• Tesla tower: kills the nearest hostile within 10 blocks (2,400 FE per shot)
• Barracks: militia, guard, archer and mage  • Vanilla walls block the way
• Crops and efficiency modules reduce pollution  • A repair kit restores 50% of a machine
There are no attacks in peaceful mode.
veio.wiki.article.climate.title: Climate and seasons
veio.wiki.article.climate.body:
The year has 4 seasons of 6 days. Temperature changes with the season (15, 25, 13 and 1 °C on average), time, altitude and rain.
• Solar: more in summer (×1.18), less in winter (×0.62)
• Wind: ×0.85 to ×1.2  • Rivers: swell in spring  • Water wheels freeze below −3 °C
• Frost stops crops below each crop's minimum temperature; under a roof (greenhouse) it counts as 20 °C
In winter it snows and lakes freeze; they thaw in spring. Power machine panels show season and temperature.
veio.wiki.article.megafactory.title: Megafactories
veio.wiki.article.megafactory.body:
Copier: build the line on the square above it and click with paper; it becomes a blueprint.
Build marker: with the blueprint, an empty hand lists the materials; sneak with the wrench to build, paying the materials.
Blueprints keep orientation and settings (filters, priorities), without copying inventories.
Floors: haulers climb ladders; the cargo lift carries items between floors.
veio.wiki.article.help.title: Troubleshooting
veio.wiki.article.help.body:
Hover over the machine panel status: it tells you why it stopped.
• No power: generator fuel, touching cables, pole reach
• Output full: carry products away from the red frame
• No material: check the input (green strips) and belt direction
• Paused: a redstone signal is reaching it
• Orange belt: truly stuck (the target refuses). A belt entering the red face is not accepted.
• Worker missing: the villager is far, in an unloaded chunk or dead; hire again
Commands: /veiotutorial ocultar · mostrar · reiniciar · noite · vila · crescer · industria · cidade. Wiki: J key.
veio.onboarding.mayor.name: Mayor Otávio
veio.onboarding.intro.home.1: You are the founder of this village's first factory. It lives off the land and wants to grow with your industry.
veio.onboarding.intro.home.2: Goal of the game: build production lines that run on their own, fill the village orders and turn it into a town.
veio.onboarding.intro.home.3: Now: walk to your house, north of the square. The bar above your hotbar shows the distance and direction.
veio.onboarding.intro.goal.home_wait: Your house is being built near the village... look around the square meanwhile.
veio.onboarding.intro.house.1: This is your house. The bed beside the panel is where you respawn: sleep in it on the first night.
veio.onboarding.intro.house.2: The panel is the control center: it shows the village, the goals and the factory report.
veio.onboarding.intro.house.3: The Hearth, where the fireplace is, warms the house and cooks. Holding a bowl, click it to eat at home.
veio.onboarding.intro.mayor.1: The mayor is in the square, with his name above his head. Right-click him.
veio.onboarding.intro.goal.mayor_here: Talk to the mayor: right-click him
veio.onboarding.mayor.hello.1: A stranger! Welcome. We live off the land here, but the land alone is no longer enough.
veio.onboarding.mayor.hello.2: Under these hills runs a vein of copper and iron that never ends. My grandfather followed it with a pickaxe; with machines it becomes plates, gears, jobs and food on the table.
veio.onboarding.mayor.hello.3: Here is my deal: the village gives the land, the workers and the orders. You build the factory, and it pays the village.
veio.onboarding.mayor.hello.4: Our workshop has the parts of a generator, the first machine. We lack the materials. Bring me:
veio.onboarding.mayor.plot: I set aside your workshop plot, %s blocks %s: %s x %s blocks marked with green sparkles. Make it all flat.
veio.onboarding.intro.plot.1: Workshop plot: centre at %s %s %s, %s blocks wide. The level is the middle height of the plot.
veio.onboarding.intro.plot.2: Small flames: extra dirt or blocks, dig them (shovel or pickaxe). Blue sparks: holes or water, fill them with dirt or stone.
veio.onboarding.intro.plot.3: Trees on the plot must go too. The bar above your hotbar counts what is left; when you finish, the mayor lets you know.
veio.onboarding.mayor.plot_again: The plot is %s blocks %s. Still %s columns to flatten: flames, dig; blue sparks, fill.
veio.onboarding.mayor.plot_done.1: What a fine floor! This is your workshop.
veio.onboarding.mayor.plot_done.2: Put the generator on the plot and the press beside it, linked by cables. Then the extractor on the ore, and belts carrying the copper to the press.
veio.onboarding.outro.goal: Go back to the mayor %s  %s blocks
veio.onboarding.outro.title: Factory founded!
veio.onboarding.mayor.next.1: Look at what you did: power, two lines, the village plan, the first paid order and a tidy home. Congratulations, engineer!
veio.onboarding.mayor.next.2: Now the village will ask for more, and every bigger order gets stuck somewhere: not enough ore, power, coal, food or people.
veio.onboarding.mayor.next.3: The next board phase asks for 32 gears. One press will not keep up: the board shows where the line waits.
veio.onboarding.mayor.next.4: And you do not have to do it all alone: with the order emeralds, the village hires people to work with you.
veio.onboarding.mayor.next.5: Come back any time: I will tell you what the village needs and what will get stuck next.
veio.onboarding.intro.village.1: You arrived in a land with no industry. There is a village nearby, and it needs someone who can build machines.
veio.onboarding.intro.village.2: Follow the arrow above your hotbar to the village.
veio.onboarding.intro.goal.village_wait: Looking for the nearest village... explore a little.
veio.onboarding.intro.arrived_sub: Find the mayor in the square
veio.onboarding.mayor.hello.5: (The house north of the square is yours: the bed beside the panel is where you respawn.)
veio.onboarding.mayor.how.1: How to get them: planks from trees, a crafting table and a wooden pickaxe; with it, break stone to get cobblestone.
veio.onboarding.mayor.how.2: With cobblestone, make a stone pickaxe and a furnace. Iron and copper ore are on hillsides and in caves.
veio.onboarding.mayor.how.3: Smelt the ore in the furnace, with coal or wood, to get ingots. Keep some coal: the generator burns coal.
veio.onboarding.intro.gather_sub: So the mayor can build the generator
veio.onboarding.intro.goal.deliver: All set! Take it to the mayor %s  %s blocks
veio.onboarding.mayor.machine.1: Done, I built your generator with my own hands. The press and the cables I don't have: when the time comes I'll tell you who has them.
veio.onboarding.mayor.machine.2: But machines cannot go just anywhere. Machines, cables and belts need flat ground.
veio.onboarding.mayor.plot_done.3: The tutorial shows each step. And whenever you do not know what to do, come talk to me.
veio.onboarding.mayor.board.none: I have not seen your Factory board yet. Make one (chest, 2 copper ingots and a stick) and put it near the machines.
veio.onboarding.mayor.board.phase: The village is in the %s phase: deliver %s %s at the Factory board.
veio.onboarding.mayor.board.grow: If the line cannot keep up, it is not lack of effort: it is a bottleneck. See on the board what stopped and double that part.
veio.onboarding.mayor.board.done: You took the village to the end of the plan. Now it is about growing: more lines, more people, more town.
veio.village.why.0: The factory runs on its own, but a village needs hands. A hired villager works without power: they eat and walk. Start with food: a farmer post in the middle of a crop field.
veio.village.do.0.1: 1. Craft the farmer post (card above). Emeralds come from trading with villagers.
veio.village.do.0.2: 2. Find or plant a wheat, carrot or potato field (up to 9x9) near the village.
veio.village.do.0.3: 3. Place the post in the middle of the field: it works its own layer, the one below and the one above.
veio.village.do.0.4: 4. Open the post with an empty hand: food on the left, harvest on the right.
veio.village.goal.0: Place a farmer post in a field
veio.village.done.0: Good spot. Now it needs someone to work it.
veio.village.why.1: Hiring costs one emerald, and the worker eats: each task costs 2 food points. Bread is worth 6 and pays for 3 harvests; raw wheat is worth 1 and pays for none.
veio.village.do.1.1: 1. Put food in the post's left slot (bread, carrots, potatoes, cooked meat).
veio.village.do.1.2: 2. Bring an adult villager within 8 blocks of the post (jobless ones are chosen first).
veio.village.do.1.3: 3. With an emerald in hand, right-click the post. The nearest one is hired.
veio.village.do.1.4: 4. If nobody is free, you keep the emerald. Sneak + wrench dismisses the worker.
veio.village.goal.1: Hire a villager at the post (emerald + right-click)
veio.village.done.1: Our first village worker! Now let us tell them where to work.
veio.village.why.2: Without a marker, the farmer only tends a square around the post. With a field marker the zone is yours: it starts at 9x9 and grows to 21x21 as the village works it.
veio.village.do.2.2: 2. Place the marker at the centre of the crop field, inside the green sparks around the post.
veio.village.do.2.3: 3. Put the seed to plant in the marker: it is the farmers' filter.
veio.village.do.2.4: 4. Later, the wrench on the marker picks the size among the unlocked levels.
veio.village.goal.2: Place a field marker near the post
veio.village.done.2: The zone is marked. Let us see the work pay off.
veio.village.why.3: The worker walks to a ripe plant, harvests, replants and brings the crop to the post. Slower than a machine, but no power needed.
veio.village.do.3.1: 1. Keep food in the post and plants growing in the zone.
veio.village.do.3.2: 2. Open the post: the panel shows the worker's state and how many harvests the food pays for.
veio.village.do.3.3: 3. If they stop, hover over the status: "no food", "nothing ripe", "path blocked"...
veio.village.done.3: The village food is secured. Now let us save you some trips.
veio.village.why.4: A hauler feeds the machines within 6 blocks of their post with what you leave on the left, and brings products to the right. A belt that walks.
veio.village.do.4.2: 2. Place it within 6 blocks of the machines it will serve (the press, for example).
veio.village.do.4.3: 3. Food and inputs on the left; hire with an emerald, as with the farmer.
veio.village.do.4.4: 4. They do not touch belts: use both where it makes sense.
veio.village.goal.4: Hire a hauler near the machines
veio.village.done.4: Now the machines have someone to feed them. We still need someone to look after the workers.
veio.village.why.5: The foreman looks after up to 6 posts within 12 blocks of the desk: brings food to those running low, rehires empty posts and plans what haulers carry from place to place.
veio.village.do.5.2: 2. Place the desk within 12 blocks of the posts (farmer and hauler).
veio.village.do.5.3: 3. Leave bread and a few emeralds on the desk: they are for the posts and for rehiring.
veio.village.do.5.4: 4. Hire the foreman with an emerald.
veio.village.goal.5: Hire a foreman near the posts
veio.village.done.5: The worker village runs itself. Now, the village of people.
veio.village.why.6: Villagers living near a house become a family: workers earn wages, the family eats from the pantry and shops. Place houses wherever you like; spread districts live better.
veio.village.do.6.2: 2. Place it within 10 blocks of where villagers stay: up to 4 live in it.
veio.village.do.6.3: 3. Put food in the pantry (3 slots). Open the house to see residents, income and HDI.
veio.village.do.6.4: 4. Avoid more than 6 neighbour houses within 16 blocks and nearby pollution: it hurts housing.
veio.village.done.6: Our first family! Now the village needs a government.
veio.village.why.7: I look after the village, but I need an office. The town hall measures population, jobs, GDP, HDI and Gini, collects tax at source and unlocks the phases: Hamlet, Village, City and Metropolis.
veio.village.do.7.2: 2. Place it at the village centre: it sees 128 blocks around.
veio.village.do.7.3: 3. Hire a villager as my clerk with an emerald: they do the office's hard work.
veio.village.do.7.4: 4. Click the town hall with a book: the report shows the problems and the next phase goal.
veio.village.recipe.0: Recipe · Farmer post (crafting table, any position): Composter + Iron hoe + Emerald + Barrel = 1× Farmer post
veio.village.recipe.2: Recipe · Field marker (crafting table, any position): Oak fence + Wheat seeds + Stick = 1× Field marker
veio.village.recipe.4: Recipe · Hauler post (crafting table, any position): Chest + Hopper + Emerald + Iron plate = 1× Hauler post
veio.village.recipe.5: Recipe · Foreman desk (crafting table, any position): Lectern + 2× Emerald + Bell = 1× Foreman desk
veio.village.recipe.6: Recipe · House (crafting table, any position): 4× Oak planks + Oak door + Glass pane = 1× House
veio.village.recipe.7: Recipe · Town hall (crafting table, any position): Bell + Lectern + Emerald + 2× Stone bricks = 1× Town hall
veio.village.from.0: Where from: emerald = trade with villagers · hoe = 2 iron + 2 sticks · composter = 7 wooden slabs · barrel = 6 planks + 2 slabs.
veio.village.from.2: Where from: fence = planks and sticks · seeds = break grass.
veio.village.from.4: Where from: iron plate = raw iron in the press · hopper = 5 iron + chest.
veio.village.from.5: Where from: lectern = 4 slabs + bookshelf · bell = village trade or villages.
veio.village.from.6: Where from: planks = logs · door = 6 planks · glass pane = 6 glass.
veio.village.from.7: Where from: stone bricks = 4 stone (smelted cobblestone) · lectern and bell as for the foreman desk.
veio.village.intro.1: The factory is up. Now comes my favourite part: the village. People working, families, a government.
veio.village.intro.2: Eight steps. I explain each one and you see it in the world. Click me whenever you want me to repeat.
veio.village.offer: When you want to learn the village (hiring, zones, houses and the town hall), talk to me again.
veio.village.end.1: Done: you hire, mark, organize, house and govern. The rest is growing.
veio.village.end.2: When you want to turn the village into a town (services, trade, money and the first phase), talk to me again.
veio.village.end.3: I will receive visitors asking for festivals and works. Keep an eye on the chat and the town hall.
veio.village.end.4: Questions? Press J: the wiki has everything. And the town hall book shows what the next phase needs.
veio.city.why.0: A town starts with clean water. Without sanitation families fall ill and HDI stays low; from the Village phase on, a new house only gets a permit with a well within 24 blocks.
veio.city.do.0.2: 2. Place it within 24 blocks of the houses: one well serves the whole district.
veio.city.do.0.3: 3. The well slot fills buckets: an empty bucket goes in, a water bucket comes out.
veio.city.do.0.4: 4. Open a house: the services line shows sanitation.
veio.city.done.0: Clean water. Now families need somewhere to shop.
veio.city.why.1: Families earn wages and spend at the nearest shop. The merchant is independent: buys from you wholesale (75% of the price) and sells retail.
veio.city.do.1.2: 2. Place it near the houses (from the City phase on, a new house needs a shop within 40 blocks).
veio.city.do.1.3: 3. Hire a merchant with an emerald, as with the posts.
veio.city.do.1.4: 4. Click the merchant: it is the Minecraft trade screen, with real stock and the local price.
veio.city.goal.1: Hire a merchant at the shop
veio.city.done.1: The shop is open. It needs goods.
veio.city.why.2: What you put in the stock the merchant buys on credit and pays from sales. Prices are local: they rise when goods are short and fall when they pile up.
veio.city.do.2.1: 1. Stock the shop with food (bread, baked potatoes) and goods (wool, leather, candles).
veio.city.do.2.2: 2. Hoppers and haulers also stock it: the shop takes automatic deliveries.
veio.city.do.2.3: 3. During the day families come to buy. Each sale withholds 4% tax for the town hall.
veio.city.do.2.4: 4. Open the shop to see the till, the prices and what sells most.
veio.city.goal.2: First sale: stock the shop and wait for daytime
veio.city.done.2: Money has started to move. Let us see where it comes from.
veio.city.why.3: The company is you: it pays your workers' wages and receives wholesale from the shops. Money only enters the village as real emeralds, through the control center vault.
veio.city.do.3.1: 1. Go to the control center (the panel in your house).
veio.city.do.3.2: 2. Put emeralds in the vault: each one becomes 60 coins in the company account.
veio.city.do.3.3: 3. Without a balance, workers go unpaid and families get poorer.
veio.city.do.3.4: 4. Click the company line on the panel to withdraw, if you need to.
veio.city.goal.3: Company account: %s coins (put emeralds in the control center vault)
veio.city.done.3: Wages secured. Now, comfort at home.
veio.city.why.4: Power is a public service: it counts in HDI with sanitation, trade and leisure. From the City phase on, a new house needs a pole within 12 blocks.
veio.city.do.4.1: 1. Craft poles (card above; the recipe makes 2).
veio.city.do.4.2: 2. Run a pole line from the factory to the district: they link on their own within 8 blocks.
veio.city.do.4.3: 3. One pole within 12 blocks of the house is enough.
veio.city.done.4: Lights at home. We still need a place to relax.
veio.city.why.5: People who only work are not happy. Parks, plazas and monuments give leisure within 32 blocks: the fourth HDI service, and village morale rises at festivals.
veio.city.do.5.2: 2. Place it within 32 blocks of the houses.
veio.city.do.5.3: 3. Later I will ask for civic works for districts without leisure: the town hall pays the company.
veio.city.do.5.4: 4. The park panel shows how many houses it serves.
veio.city.done.5: A park! Now we need more people.
veio.city.why.6: A real village has several families. Each house holds up to 4 villagers; babies are born where there is room. Houses packed too tight are crowded: spread the district.
veio.city.do.6.2: 2. Place them near villagers, with at most 6 neighbours within 16 blocks.
veio.city.do.6.3: 3. Free beds make the village grow; food in the pantry keeps families going.
veio.city.do.6.4: 4. Open the town hall: it shows families, jobs and the village HDI.
veio.city.done.6: Three families! The village has a district.
veio.city.title.7: Growth 8 of 10 · Taxes and the public account
veio.city.why.7: I make nothing: the town hall lives on the tax withheld from each sale (4% now, up to 16% in a Metropolis). With it I pay clerks, wells, aid to the poor and public works.
veio.city.do.7.1: 1. Go to the town hall and open the panel: it shows the public account.
veio.city.do.7.2: 2. Click it with a book: the report shows the money in circulation per account.
veio.city.do.7.3: 3. Every shop sale leaves a share here. Nothing vanishes: money only changes account.
veio.city.do.7.4: 4. The town hall emerald slot takes a voluntary contribution from you.
veio.city.goal.7: Public account: %s coins (tax arrives with every sale)
veio.city.done.7: The public account has money. That is how the village keeps going.

veio.city.intro.1: The village works. Now let us make it a good place to live: water, trade, money, light, leisure, festivals and more families.
veio.city.intro.2: Ten steps. At the end the village moves up a phase, and the master plan unlocks more villagers, bigger zones and more houses.
veio.city.start_sub: Services, trade, money, festivals and the first phase
veio.city.end.1: Water, trade, wages, tax, light, leisure, festivals and families: you know how to build a town.
veio.city.end.2: For City: 36 residents, 9 families, HDI 0.55, GDP of 400 a day and 60% employment. The town hall report tracks each number.
veio.city.end.3: For Metropolis: 80 residents, 20 families, HDI 0.70, 3 districts and Gini up to 0.45: income well spread across families.
veio.city.end.4: With the cargo port or station, the village sells to the world: contracts pay more and open new markets. See the Foreign trade tab at the control center.
veio.city.hint.0: The well only counts for houses with residents within 24 blocks. Move the well to the middle of the district, or wait for the family to form.
veio.city.hint.1: To hire you need a free adult villager within 8 blocks of the shop and an emerald in hand. Bring a villager closer, or free up a worker.
veio.city.hint.2: Families only buy during the day and with money in their wallet. Without wages (empty company account) nobody buys: put emeralds in the control center vault.
veio.city.hint.3: The vault is the emerald slot of the control center. Emeralds come from villager trades, the contract hub and exports.
veio.city.hint.4: The pole must be within 12 blocks of a house with residents. It does not need a generator to count, but the factory will thank you.
veio.city.hint.5: The park takes a few seconds to register and only serves houses within 32 blocks. Place it in the middle of the district.
veio.city.hint.6: A family forms with villagers within 10 blocks of the house. With no spare villagers, the village grows with free beds: put beds near the houses.
veio.city.hint.7: The public account only receives when the shop sells. Check that the shop has stock and families have wages.
veio.city.why.8: The year has seasons, Sundays and holidays. Two days before each one, a visitor comes to the town hall asking for what the festival needs. A prepared festival raises morale, and morale weighs on HDI.
veio.city.do.8.1: 1. When chat says a visitor arrived, go to the town hall and click them.
veio.city.do.8.2: 2. They tell you what they need: the bar shows the request and what is missing.
veio.city.do.8.3: 3. Deliver the items in the town hall's 3rd slot (Agenda). The town hall reimburses the company.
veio.city.do.8.4: 4. The panel Agenda tab (arrows in the title) shows the calendar, morale and requests.
veio.city.done.8: Festival ready! The village will celebrate on the day.
veio.city.hint.8: Visitors arrive 2 days before each Sunday or holiday. Meanwhile, gather cooked food: almost every festival asks for bread, cake or cookies.
veio.city.title.9: Growth 10 of 10 · Move up a phase
veio.city.why.9: The master plan has four phases: Hamlet, Village, City and Metropolis. To become a Village: 12 residents, 3 families and HDI 0.40. I check at the end of each day.
veio.city.do.9.1: 1. Open the town hall or click it with a book: the report says what is missing.
veio.city.do.9.2: 2. The bar shows the weakest part of HDI: food, housing, services or income.
veio.city.do.9.3: 3. Residents grow with free beds and houses with room.
veio.city.do.9.4: 4. In the Village phase, zones can reach level 3, the village 60 villagers and 10 houses, and tax rises to 8%.
veio.city.done.9: We are a Village! The master plan moved forward.
veio.city.hint.9: The phase only changes at the end of the day, with the town hall clerk present. If everything is past the goal, sleep a night and check again.
veio.city.goal.8_wait: Festival: the next visitor arrives in %s day(s) (%s). Meanwhile, gather cooked food
veio.city.fix.0: Food: put cooked food in house pantries and in the shop; bread and baked potatoes are worth more than raw wheat.
veio.city.fix.1: Housing: crowded houses and pollution hurt. Spread the houses and keep the district away from polluting machines.
veio.city.fix.2: Services: check well, pole, shop and leisure near each house. Open a house to see which is missing.
veio.city.fix.3: Income: more employed villagers and wages paid. Hire at posts and keep emeralds in the company vault.
veio.city.end.5: I will be at the town hall. Click me whenever you want the factory's next step.
veio.city.goal.8_soon: Festival: a visitor will soon arrive at the town hall

veio.night.first.1: It is dark! Nobody stays outside here at night: monsters come out and hunt whoever is outdoors.
veio.night.first.2: Go to your house, north of the plaza. Sleep in the bed next to the panel and the night passes in a moment.
veio.night.first.3: Work can wait for dawn. Tomorrow we will talk about making the village safer.
veio.night.goal.inside: Home and safe. Sleep in the bed to skip the night
veio.night.goal.shelter: Night! Take shelter: stay somewhere with a door and light until dawn
veio.night.dawn_sub: You made it through the first night
veio.night.dawn: Good morning! See how the village shuts in? Every night is like that. One day we will have walls and guards; until then, home at dusk.
veio.night.dusk.1: The village bell rang: it is getting dark. Villagers shut their doors.
veio.night.dusk.2: Night is falling. Out there, monsters are stirring. Time to head back.
veio.night.dusk.3: The sun has set. Those working outside go home; the factory runs on its own.
veio.night.dusk.4: It is dark. Light and walls are a village's best company at night.
veio.night.offer: Whenever you like, talk to me again: before growing, the village needs to lose its fear of the night.
veio.night.start_sub: Light, walls and a peaceful night
veio.night.intro.1: The village fears the night, and rightly so: monsters hunt whoever is outside, and as the factory grows worse things will come.
veio.night.intro.2: Before growing, let us make the village sleep in peace: light, walls and beds. Then the factory: what it pollutes, its wall and our defense plan.
veio.night.title.0: Night 1 of 6 · Light in the village
veio.night.why.0: Monsters spawn in the dark. A lit village is a village where they do not appear: every torch is a patch of safe ground.
veio.night.do.0.1: 1. Make torches (coal or charcoal + stick) or lanterns.
veio.night.do.0.2: 2. Place them in the plaza, the streets and around the houses (within 40 blocks of the village centre).
veio.night.do.0.3: 3. Spread them out: a torch every 6 or 7 blocks leaves no dark corner.
veio.night.do.0.4: 4. The factory too: a monster near machines is trouble.
veio.night.done.0: What a lovely village at night! And much safer.
veio.night.why.1: Light keeps them away, a wall keeps them out. Monsters walk, they do not climb: a wall around the village and the factory stops almost everything, including the Raiders that will come one day.
veio.night.do.1.1: 1. Build a wall around the village: stone walls, fences or stone blocks (between 12 and 64 blocks from the centre).
veio.night.do.1.2: 2. Two blocks high is enough for walkers; walls and fences count as tall.
veio.night.do.1.3: 3. Leave a gate (fence gate) or a door for you and the villagers.
veio.night.do.1.4: 4. Include the factory: it is what will attract Raiders once it pollutes.
veio.night.done.1: A wall! Now the village can breathe at night.
veio.night.why.2: Night is not for working outside. The factory runs on its own; you rest and wake up to the work done. Sleeping also makes the night pass.
veio.night.do.2.1: 1. At dusk, get back inside the wall.
veio.night.do.2.2: 2. Sleep in your house bed (or any bed, at night).
veio.night.do.2.3: 3. Civilian workers sleep too; the barracks, once built, stays on watch.
veio.night.done.2: Good morning! That is how it is done: the village slept in peace.
veio.night.goal.2_day: A peaceful night: when it gets dark, sleep in the bed
veio.night.goal.2_night: Night! Get inside the wall and sleep in the bed
veio.night.more.0: Learn more: J → Systems → Pollution and defense.
veio.night.more.1: Learn more: J → Systems → Pollution and defense (waves and walls).
veio.night.more.2: Learn more: J → Systems → Worker village (workers resting).
veio.night.end.1: Light, walls and beds: the village sleeps soundly. But remember: the more the factory makes, the more it pollutes.
veio.night.end.2: With high pollution come the Raiders, at night and in waves. There is no way around it: to supply the village and the world, the factory will pollute.
veio.night.end.3: That is why defense grows with the factory. Now talk to me whenever you like: the village needs hands.
veio.night.title.3: Night 4 of 6 · The price of the factory
veio.night.why.3: Every working machine pollutes its chunk, and the generator most of all. Pollution spreads and only part of it fades. It is what will one day call the Raiders.
veio.night.do.3.1: 1. Open a working machine (the generator, for example) with an empty hand: the panel shows pollution per minute.
veio.night.do.3.2: 2. The bar shows the workshop chunk pollution: the warning comes at 400; waves above 1,200.
veio.night.do.3.3: 3. Crops absorb pollution with every harvest; the efficiency module cuts it in half.
veio.night.do.3.4: 4. You cannot avoid polluting: you can plan for it.
veio.night.goal.3: Workshop pollution: %s · warning at %s · waves above %s · open a polluting machine
veio.night.done.3: Now you read the danger before it arrives.
veio.night.why.4: Raiders go after whoever is at the factory and, with nobody around, strike the polluting machine. Four blows stop a machine. The workshop needs a wall too.
veio.night.do.4.1: 1. Fence the workshop: walls, fences or stone between 4 and 24 blocks from the generator.
veio.night.do.4.2: 2. Leave a gate for you and the haulers.
veio.night.do.4.3: 3. Belts leaving the workshop go through the gate or, later, under the wall with the belt tunnel.
veio.night.do.4.4: 4. Light up inside the wall: monsters do not spawn on lit ground.
veio.night.done.4: The workshop is walled. Come talk to me: I have a plan.
veio.night.why.5: Walls and light hold the beginning. When the factory grows, we will need more. Come to the plaza: I want to show you the plan, and where each defense fails.
veio.night.do.5.1: 1. Talk to mayor Otávio in the plaza.
veio.night.do.5.2: 2. He explains the waves, the barracks and the Tesla tower: what each costs and where it fails.
veio.night.do.5.3: 3. You cannot build them yet: the barracks comes with circuits, and the Tesla with the electronics research.
veio.night.goal.5: Talk to the mayor in the plaza: the defense council
veio.night.done.5: Advice given. May the village sleep in peace.
veio.night.council.1: Sit down. To supply the village and, one day, the world, the factory will pollute; there is no other way. And pollution brings Raiders.
veio.night.council.2: The signal: above 400 I warn you in chat. A day later, on nights when pollution passes 1,200, the waves come: 4 Raiders the first time, up to 12.
veio.night.council.3: From the 3rd attack night come archers; from the 5th, the Brute: slow, tough, goes straight for the machines and hits twice as hard. Four blows stop a machine, until a repair kit.
veio.night.council.4: With circuits you raise the barracks: one soldier per building. Militia arrives fast, the guard holds and heals, the archer shoots from afar, the mage hits two.
veio.night.council.5: The barracks weakness: the soldier eats with every blow. With no food in the barracks, nobody leaves their post. And changing class costs an emerald.
veio.night.council.6: Later, with the electronics research, comes the Tesla tower: it kills the nearest monster on its own, within 10 blocks. But each shot costs 2,400 FE and it stores 20,000: that is 8 shots, one every 2 seconds.
veio.night.council.7: The Tesla weakness: at night solar gives nothing. Without batteries or a generator it goes dark mid-wave. And a coal generator pollutes... and calls more Raiders.
veio.night.council.8: That is the defense game: walls, food in the barracks and energy saved for the night. I will keep reminding you. For today, the village is ready.
veio.night.more.3: Learn more: J → Systems → Pollution and defense (the meter and the waves).
veio.night.more.4: Learn more: J → Systems → Pollution and defense (what Raiders attack).
veio.night.more.5: Learn more: J → Systems → Pollution and defense (barracks, Tesla and their bottlenecks).
veio.forge.why.0: The Factory board is the industry plan: each phase asks for a stack only a working line delivers. The Workshop asks for 32 gears; Steel, 16 steel plates.
veio.forge.do.0.1: 1. Make the Factory board (chest, 2 copper ingots and a stick) and place it near the machines.
veio.forge.do.0.2: 2. Deliver 32 gears: unlocks the wrench, crusher, alloy furnace and repair kit.
veio.forge.do.0.3: 3. Alloy furnace: 2 iron plates + coal = 1 steel plate. Deliver 16.
veio.forge.do.0.4: 4. Bottleneck: the gear line draws 40 FE/t, more than one water wheel. Plan the power.
veio.forge.done.0: Steel! The factory became an industry.
veio.forge.more.0: Learn more: J → Systems → Phases and research.
veio.forge.why.1: A circuit is copper turned smart: wire in the cutter, silicon in the crusher or alloy furnace, and the circuit assembler.
veio.forge.do.1.1: 1. Cutter: copper plate becomes wire. Crusher: quartz becomes silicon (or 4 sand + coal in the alloy furnace).
veio.forge.do.1.3: 3. Deliver 16 circuits at the board: unlocks solar, Mk.II, modules and the barracks.
veio.forge.do.1.4: 4. Bottleneck: silicon. Without the Nether, the sand route is longer, but it works.
veio.forge.more.1: Learn more: J → Systems → Phases and research.
veio.forge.why.2: The Mk.II mines one unit per second, twice the basic one, and reaches diamond and emerald. With it the line doubles, and so does pollution: 4 per second.
veio.forge.do.2.1: 1. Craft the Mk.II (card above): it uses a basic extractor.
veio.forge.do.2.2: 2. Swap the extractor on a good vein for the Mk.II.
veio.forge.do.2.3: 3. Double what comes after: two presses per Mk.II, a fast belt if needed.
veio.forge.do.2.4: 4. See on the panel how much it pollutes per minute.
veio.forge.done.2: Twice the ore. The village is grateful, and the air feels it.
veio.forge.more.2: Learn more: J → Systems → Deposits and extraction.
veio.forge.why.3: With a bigger factory, pollution passes 400 and I warn you in chat. A day later, on nights it passes 1,200, the waves begin. It is the price of growing.
veio.forge.do.3.1: 1. Let the factory work: the bar shows the most polluted chunk.
veio.forge.do.3.2: 2. When the warning comes, check the wall, the light and the factory gate.
veio.forge.do.3.3: 3. Nearby crops absorb; the efficiency module halves it. But to supply the village, it will pollute.
veio.forge.do.3.4: 4. Get ready: the next steps are defense.
veio.forge.done.3: There is the warning. Now, defense.
veio.forge.more.3: Learn more: J → Systems → Pollution and defense.
veio.forge.why.4: Walls stop walkers; the barracks fights. One soldier per building, on watch at night too. They eat with every blow: with no food, nobody leaves their post.
veio.forge.do.4.1: 1. Craft the barracks (card above) and place it inside the wall, near the factory.
veio.forge.do.4.2: 2. Food in the left slot; an emerald in the right one, for wages.
veio.forge.do.4.3: 3. Hire with an emerald; sneak with an emerald to change class.
veio.forge.do.4.4: 4. Militia is fast, the guard holds and heals, the archer shoots from afar, the mage hits two.
veio.forge.done.4: We have a soldier. The village sleeps easier.
veio.forge.more.4: Learn more: J → Systems → Worker village (barracks).
veio.forge.why.5: The Tesla defends on its own: it kills the nearest monster within 10 blocks. But each shot costs 2,400 FE and it stores 20,000, just 8 shots. Power is its bottleneck.
veio.forge.do.5.1: 1. The recipe comes from the electronics research: 128 circuits and 128 frames in the lab.
veio.forge.do.5.2: 2. Place the tower near the polluting machines: that is where Raiders go.
veio.forge.do.5.3: 3. Connect it to the grid (cable or pole): it only fires with stored energy.
veio.forge.do.5.4: 4. It does not hit villagers, animals or bosses.
veio.forge.done.5: The Tesla is charged. Now, the night.
veio.forge.more.5: Learn more: J → Systems → Pollution and defense (bottlenecks).
veio.forge.title.6: Industry 7 of 8 · Power for the night
veio.forge.why.6: At night solar gives nothing. Without a reserve, the Tesla goes dark mid-wave. Each battery stores 30,000 FE; a coal generator holds, but it pollutes and calls more waves.
veio.forge.do.6.2: 2. Connect them to the Tesla grid, with cable or pole.
veio.forge.do.6.3: 3. Charge them by day, with spare power.
veio.forge.do.6.4: 4. Quick math: a wave of 12 needs 12 shots, 28,800 FE. One Tesla alone is not enough.
veio.forge.why.7: Four blows stop a machine, and the Brute hits twice as hard. A stopped machine keeps its stock: a repair kit, right-clicked, restores 50%.
veio.forge.do.7.3: 3. After a wave, walk the factory: the panel shows each machine's integrity.
veio.forge.more.7: Learn more: J → Systems → Pollution and defense.
veio.forge.intro.1: The village grew and asks for more: more plates, more gears, more food. Today's workshop cannot keep up.
veio.forge.intro.2: Let us take the factory to steel and electronics, with the Mk.II extractor. But making more means polluting more.
veio.forge.intro.3: And pollution brings Raiders. This time defense comes along: barracks, Tesla tower and power for the night.
veio.forge.end.1: The factory became an industry, and the village has a defense.
veio.forge.end.2: Waves will return, bigger with pollution: up to 12 Raiders, archers and the Brute. More Teslas, more power, more soldiers.
veio.forge.end.3: With industry standing, the village can become a city. Talk to me whenever you like.
veio.forge.end.4: And remember: the Factory board always tells you the next bottleneck.

veio.metro.why.0: A city needs people. Each house holds up to 4; babies are born where there is a free bed and room at home. In the Village phase, the village can have up to 60 villagers and 10 houses.
veio.metro.do.0.1: 1. Build more houses, in spread districts (at most 6 neighbours within 16 blocks).
veio.metro.do.0.2: 2. Free beds near houses make the village grow.
veio.metro.do.0.3: 3. A new house needs a well within 24 blocks (the Village phase permit).
veio.metro.do.0.4: 4. Food in the pantries keeps families going.
veio.metro.done.0: Nine families! The village already looks like a city.
veio.metro.more.0: Learn more: J → Systems → Village society (houses and families).
veio.metro.why.1: A family without wages gets poorer, and HDI falls. The City asks for 60% of adults employed: posts, shops, barracks and the town hall count.
veio.metro.do.1.1: 1. Hire at work posts: farmer, shepherd, hauler, foreman.
veio.metro.do.1.2: 2. Shops and the barracks employ too.
veio.metro.do.1.3: 3. The company account must pay: emeralds in the vault.
veio.metro.do.1.4: 4. Open the town hall: it shows village employment.
veio.metro.more.1: Learn more: J → Systems → Economy and money (wages).
veio.metro.why.2: In a City, every house counts. Sanitation, power, trade and leisure for every family: it weighs most on HDI. From the City phase, a new house also needs a pole within 12 blocks.
veio.metro.do.2.1: 1. Open each house: the services line says what is missing.
veio.metro.do.2.2: 2. Well within 24, pole within 12, shop within 40 and leisure within 32 blocks.
veio.metro.do.2.3: 3. Far districts need their own services.
veio.metro.do.2.4: 4. The bar shows how many houses have everything.
veio.metro.more.2: Learn more: J → Systems → Village society (services and HDI).
veio.metro.why.3: A district without leisure asks for a work. Every 4 days I ask for a park, a plaza or a monument for the neediest district, and the town hall pays the company for it.
veio.metro.do.3.1: 1. When the request arrives, the bar shows what and where.
veio.metro.do.3.2: 2. Build the civic block within 32 blocks of the district, within 6 days.
veio.metro.do.3.3: 3. Park 240, plaza 420, monument 720 coins, paid to the company.
veio.metro.do.3.4: 4. Work done: morale +10 and permanent leisure in the district.
veio.metro.done.3: Work delivered. The city has its own face.
veio.metro.more.3: Learn more: J → Systems → Calendar, holidays and civic works.
veio.metro.why.4: The village GDP is what families buy per day, plus what the village exports. For a City: 400 a day. More people with wages, more stocked shops, more GDP.
veio.metro.do.4.1: 1. Shops always stocked: an empty stock sells nothing.
veio.metro.do.4.2: 2. Wages paid: a family without money does not buy.
veio.metro.do.4.3: 3. Goods beyond food (wool, leather, candles, books) raise what each house spends.
veio.metro.do.4.4: 4. Later, the cargo port or station adds exports.
veio.metro.more.4: Learn more: J → Systems → Economy and money.
veio.metro.why.5: Everything together, at the end of the day: 36 residents, 9 families, HDI 0.55, GDP 400 and 60% employment, with my clerk in the office. Then I declare the City.
veio.metro.do.5.1: 1. The bar lists each goal with ✔ or ✘.
veio.metro.do.5.2: 2. The town hall book shows districts and problems.
veio.metro.do.5.3: 3. In the City phase: zone level 4, 100 villagers, 24 houses and 12% tax.
veio.metro.do.5.4: 4. If everything is green, sleep a night: the phase changes at the end of the day.
veio.metro.more.5: Learn more: J → Systems → Village society (phases).
veio.metro.intro.1: Industry brought work, and work brought people. It is time for the Village to become a City.
veio.metro.intro.2: For a City: 36 residents, 9 families, HDI 0.55, GDP of 400 a day and 60% employment.
veio.metro.intro.3: One thing at a time. Let us start with families.
veio.metro.end.1: A City! From the handful of houses I governed to this.
veio.metro.end.2: A Metropolis asks for 80 residents, 20 families, HDI 0.70, 3 districts and Gini up to 0.45: income well spread.
veio.metro.end.3: The village now makes more than it consumes. Out there, people want to buy.
veio.metro.end.4: Whenever you want the next step, talk to me.

veio.onboarding.story.0: The factory first flame! Always keep coal: a cold generator is a stopped factory.
veio.onboarding.story.1: The village smith hammers one plate a day. The press makes one every second and a half.
veio.onboarding.story.2: Watch the machine work once with your own hands. After that you will never want to do it again.
veio.onboarding.story.3: One machine alone is a tool. Two chained together are already a factory.
veio.onboarding.story.4: Ore under the ground never runs out: the extractor mines it forever, as long as it has power.
veio.onboarding.story.5: This is where the magic starts: copper walks to the press on its own. You just watch.
veio.onboarding.story.6: A machine with a full output stops. Always ask: where does what it makes go?
veio.onboarding.story.7: The village needs plates and gears for its first works. It is your first order!
veio.onboarding.story.8: Now that the line runs, let us grow the village. The board is the plan we follow together.
veio.onboarding.story.9: Each phase asks for more than the last. When a delivery takes long, look at the board: it shows the bottleneck.
veio.onboarding.story.10: A good factory is not the one that works hardest, it is the one that never stops. Find what is missing and double only that part.
veio.onboarding.story.11: Two presses with one ore, or two extractors with one press: one side always waits. The splitter balances it.
veio.onboarding.story.12: One day your factory will be too big for cables. Poles carry power from one side of the village to the other.
veio.onboarding.story.13: The daily order is how the village pays the factory. With those emeralds, we hire people to work with you.
veio.onboarding.story.14: And you need to eat too! A hot meal at home and you work twice as hard.
veio.onboarding.story.15: From home you see the whole village. It is your engineer office.
veio.onboarding.story.16: You learned all I could teach. Come see me in the square.

veio.onboarding.hint.head: You have been on this step for a while. A tip:
veio.onboarding.hint.0: Open the generator with an EMPTY hand (holding an item places the block). No coal? Charcoal works: a log in the furnace.
veio.onboarding.hint.1: Cables must TOUCH, with no gap: generator, cable, cable, press. And the generator must be burning coal.
veio.onboarding.hint.2: RAW copper, not ingots: the ore broken with a stone pickaxe. It is on hillsides and just below the grass in caves.
veio.onboarding.hint.3: The assembler needs power too: a cable touching it. Two plates in the input make one gear.
veio.onboarding.hint.4: The extractor goes ON TOP of the ore, without mining it. If its bar does not fill, it lacks power or the block below is not ore.
veio.onboarding.hint.5: A belt runs away from you. Place it looking from the extractor towards the press, and the last one on a GREEN face of the press.
veio.onboarding.hint.6: The output belt starts against the RED frame (behind the press) and ends inside the chest.
veio.onboarding.hint.7: For the 8 gears, put plates in the assembler and let it work. Plates in hub input 1, gears in input 2.
veio.onboarding.hint.8: The board is already unlocked in the recipe book (green): chest, 2 copper ingots and a stick.
veio.onboarding.hint.9: The board only accepts COPPER plates in phase 1. Watch the number on its panel go up; a belt from the press does it by itself.
veio.onboarding.hint.10: Any new extractor counts, even on another ore. Power it and run a belt into the line.
veio.onboarding.hint.11: The splitter is in the book after board phase 1. It needs a gear, 2 belts and redstone (red ore in caves).
veio.onboarding.hint.12: The first pole stands within 2 blocks of the generator; the second within 8 of the first. If no wire appears, move them closer.
veio.onboarding.hint.13: The order changes every day and belongs to the whole village: open the board to see it. Sometimes it is iron plates: raw iron in the press.
veio.onboarding.hint.14: The bowl is wooden: 3 planks in a V. The Home block is inside your house, north of the square; put food in its pantry.
veio.onboarding.hint.15: The control center is the panel in your house. Click it with an empty hand.
veio.village.hint.0: Emerald: trade with the village folk. The fletcher buys sticks; the farmer buys wheat, potatoes or carrots.
veio.village.hint.1: Nobody hired? The villager must be within 8 blocks and without a post. If none, the post waits 30 s: click the villager with the emerald.
veio.village.hint.2: The marker must stand inside the green sparkles around the post, at the same height (one block up or down at most).
veio.village.hint.3: Raw wheat barely feeds: put bread in the post. And the crops must be ripe to be harvested.
veio.village.hint.4: The hauler only serves machines within 6 blocks of the post. Put supplies on the left for him to bring to the machines.
veio.village.hint.5: The foreman desk needs a free villager nearby and an emerald in hand to hire.
veio.village.hint.6: The house only gets residents if there are villagers within 10 blocks. Put food in its pantry.
veio.village.hint.7: The town hall needs a free villager and an emerald, like the posts.
veio.onboarding.diary.0:
Otávio's Diary
Mayor of the village


For the engineer who came down the dirt road.
veio.onboarding.diary.1:
The vein

My grandfather opened the first mine in these hills. He said a vein of copper and iron runs down there and never ends.

The pickaxe could not keep up. The mine closed, and the village went back to farming.
veio.onboarding.diary.2:
The deal

The village gives the land, the workers and the orders. You build the factory, and the factory pays the village.

Machines do not tire. An extractor follows the vein forever, as long as it has power.
veio.onboarding.diary.3:
The road

Act I · The first flame
Act II · The line that runs itself
Act III · The village plan
Act IV · The village counts on you

Then: the working village and the town.
veio.onboarding.diary.4:
Advice

A stopped machine has a reason: hover over its status.

A full output stops the line.

Stuck? Talk to me.

The J key opens the wiki.

veio.onboarding.title.9: Step 10 of 16 · A phase of the plan
veio.onboarding.why.9: Each board phase asks for a bigger delivery and unlocks new machines. That is how the village grows.
veio.onboarding.do.9.1: 1. The first phase asks for 16 copper plates in the board input slot.
veio.onboarding.do.9.2: 2. Even better: run a belt from the press into the board. It only accepts what the phase asks for.
veio.onboarding.do.9.3: 3. Reward: 32 belts at the board output, and the splitter, assembler and hub unlocked.
veio.onboarding.why.10: The press makes more than one basic extractor can mine. When input runs short, the bottleneck is the ore.
veio.onboarding.do.10.2: 2. Place it on top of other copper ore and bring power to it.
veio.onboarding.do.10.3: 3. Run its output by belt into the same line that goes to the press.
veio.onboarding.why.11: With ore to spare, one press becomes the bottleneck. The splitter shares one belt between two.
veio.onboarding.do.11.1: 1. Craft the splitter (card above: gear, 2 belts and redstone make 2).
veio.onboarding.do.11.2: 2. Put the splitter in the middle of the copper belt: it sends half to each side.
veio.onboarding.do.11.3: 3. Each output goes to a press. Sneaking with the wrench, it gives one side priority.
veio.onboarding.why.12: Cables are for short runs. To carry power to another part of the plot, use poles: the wire goes through the air.
veio.onboarding.do.12.1: 1. Craft wooden poles (card above: each recipe makes 2).
veio.onboarding.do.12.2: 2. Put the first within 2 blocks of the generator: it pulls power from there.
veio.onboarding.do.12.3: 3. Put the second within 8 blocks of the first: the wire appears by itself. Machines within 2 blocks of it get power.
veio.onboarding.why.13: Every day the village places an order at the board and pays in emeralds. It is the money to hire people.
veio.onboarding.do.13.1: 1. Open the board: the panel shows today order (what and how much).
veio.onboarding.do.13.2: 2. Deliver it at the board input slot, by belt if you can, alongside the phase.
veio.onboarding.do.13.3: 3. Once the order is complete, the emeralds appear at the board output. Keep them: the mayor will ask.
veio.onboarding.why.14: The Home block, inside your house, is where you rest. Eating at home gives you more strength for work.
veio.onboarding.do.14.1: 1. At the Home: wood or coal in the fireplace (first slot) and food in the pantry (slots 2 to 4).
veio.onboarding.do.14.2: 2. Holding a bowl, click the Home: a home meal. With the fire lit, you get effects.
veio.onboarding.do.14.3: 3. Varied dishes and a comfortable house (bed, light, window) make the effects stronger.
veio.onboarding.why.15: The control center, in your house, shows the whole village at once: people, food, money and works.
veio.onboarding.do.15.1: 1. Go to your house and open the control center (the panel beside the bed).
veio.onboarding.do.15.2: 2. It holds the village food, the goals, the company cash and the works.
veio.onboarding.do.15.3: 3. The Veio wiki (J key) explains each system whenever you want to know more.
veio.onboarding.why.16: You learned power, machines, belts, the board, bottlenecks, the splitter, poles, the daily order and home.
veio.onboarding.do.16.1: Next: go back to the mayor, in the village square. He tells you what comes next.
veio.onboarding.do.16.2: Expanding: one basic extractor feeds one press. More machines need more power.
